partner_result_applied.application: Its explicit C_0 height bound M_B was inserted into P(Q in I)<=M_B |I| on the separator branch.

proved_results: For any absolutely continuous R^n law and any nonzero symmetric A, X^TAX has an absolutely continuous law; independence and density cap are unnecessary for this existence statement.
The universal essential-density bound is exactly equivalent to the linear interval small-ball inequality P(Q in I)<=C|I|.
On the account04/B15 separator branch, the completed C_0 theorem yields the corresponding interval bound with its explicit matrix-dependent M_B.

new_correction.statement: Rank-three curvature plus a bounded joint density does not imply a continuous quadratic pushforward density; normalized shell input for q=|x|^2 gives a discontinuous density. This is not a product-law target counterexample.

unresolved_implication: Full universal matrix- and dimension-independent linear small-ball bound remains open; stronger continuity for fully coupled/no-separator product laws remains open and must retain product structure.
next_step: For continuity, use an original-coordinate product/bilinear-bank mechanism before projecting to a generic joint law; for the central bound, attack the fully coupled heavy-coordinate small-ball inequality.
